A compound state can resume the child that was active when it was exited by using a HistoryState.
When the compound state is exited, the HistoryState remembers which child was active.
The state machine can return to the remembered child when the compound state is resumed.

When a callback raises an exception in a StateChart, the runtime exception does not crash the machine.
In a StateChart, when a callback raises an exception, it becomes an error.execution event.
In a StateChart, an error.execution event can be handled with regular transitions.
In a StateChart, if a callback raises a RuntimeError, the machine transitions to an error state.
In a StateChart, the error can be processed in an on_enter method for the error state.
In a StateChart, if a validator raises an exception, this exception is not converted to an error.execution event.
In a StateChart, if a validator raises an exception, it does not trigger error.execution transitions.
In a StateChart, if a validator raises an exception, the exception is propagated directly to the caller.
In a StateChart, exceptions raised by validators can be handled by the caller with a try/except block.
